# AMD Instinct validation campaign for vLLM ROCm serving parity

## Description

This epic runs a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct accelerators to
establish functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
platform's supported model set, and produces the go/no-go recommendation that
determines which models are productized for ROCm serving. It resolves the
platform's lack of first-hand ROCm parity data and de-risks the productization
decision.

## Scope

- Write a validation plan that enumerates the supported model set and defines
  functional pass/fail criteria and performance parity metrics (throughput and
  latency) against the existing CUDA baseline.
- Drive securing of access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (procurement or
  partner-lab engagement) — the access process is in scope; see Risks/Notes for
  the availability caveat.
- Execute functional validation of vLLM ROCm builds per model on the AMD
  Instinct hardware, recording pass/fail with failure details.
- Execute performance parity measurement per model against the CUDA baseline.
- Produce a go/no-go report: the cleared model list, parity findings, and a
  recommendation of the productization scope for vLLM ROCm serving.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation plan exists covering the supported model set with defined
  functional pass/fail criteria and performance parity metrics.
- Functional validation results are recorded for each model in the supported
  set, run on AMD Instinct hardware with vLLM ROCm builds.
- Performance parity data (throughput and latency versus the CUDA baseline) is
  recorded for each model.
- A go/no-go report with the cleared model list and a productization scope
  recommendation is published to stakeholders.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishing functional and performance parity data and the go/no-go scope
  for productization.

## Risks / Notes

- Hardware access is unresolved (strategy open question 1). Node availability
  via procurement or partner lab is granted by parties outside the strategy and
  its timing cannot be compressed; the acceptance criteria therefore sit on the
  campaign's report deliverable, not on node availability.
- The training-side validation work also needs AMD Instinct nodes; access
  secured for this campaign should be shared (coordination risk, not a
  dependency).

# Productize vLLM ROCm serving runtime for validated models

## Description

This epic productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime — a ROCm build of
the vLLM serving runtime image plus its ServingRuntime definition — for the
models cleared by the AMD Instinct validation campaign, integrated with the
existing KServe serving stack so InferenceServices can serve those models on
AMD GPU nodes.

## Scope

- Build and publish a ROCm variant of the vLLM serving runtime image through
  the existing midstream build pipeline, pinning the upstream ROCm base image
  version used.
- Provide a ServingRuntime (or ClusterServingRuntime) definition that deploys
  the ROCm runtime on AMD GPU nodes, scoped to the campaign's cleared model
  list.
- Validate the runtime end-to-end under KServe InferenceServices on AMD
  Instinct nodes (KServe itself requires no code change; this validates the
  passive serving stack against the new runtime).
- Define the supported-state designation for the cleared models and confirm the
  existing CUDA runtime builds are unaffected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ROCm vLLM serving runtime image builds green in the build pipeline and
  is published for the platform release.
- A ServingRuntime definition deploys the ROCm runtime targeting AMD GPU
  nodes, restricted to the cleared model list.
- An InferenceService using the ROCm vLLM runtime serves a cleared model
  end-to-end on AMD Instinct nodes.
- The upstream ROCm base image version is pinned and documented.
- The cleared-model support scope is documented and the CUDA runtime builds
  are unaffected.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the
  models the validation campaign clears.

## Risks / Notes

- Scope is gated by the validation campaign's go/no-go outcome: the cleared
  model list (including a possible empty or partial list) rewrites this epic's
  supported-model scope.
- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and upstream
  communities and may not align with release trains (strategy open question 2);
  mitigation is the pinned base image version, and re-pinning if a release
  train misaligns.

# PyTorch ROCm training support via Training Operator

## Description

This epic enables PyTorch training on ROCm for jobs run through the Training
Operator: single-GPU and multi-GPU (distributed) PyTorchJobs execute on AMD
Instinct nodes using ROCm-enabled PyTorch environments, admitted through Kueue
when workload queueing is enabled.

## Scope

- Define and validate the PyTorchJob container/runtime configuration for ROCm
  (ROCm-enabled PyTorch images, AMD GPU node targeting) for the Training
  Operator's PyTorchJob CRD.
- Validate single-GPU PyTorchJob execution on AMD Instinct nodes.
- Validate multi-GPU distributed PyTorchJob execution (all workers on AMD
  GPUs) on AMD Instinct nodes.
- Validate that PyTorchJobs requesting `amd.com/gpu` are admitted and run
  through Kueue queueing end-to-end (the quota-side configuration is owned by
  the Kueue amd.com/gpu quota workstream; this epic covers the job side).
- Document the required job configuration for submitting ROCm training jobs
  (incidental reference documentation that falls out of the implementation).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob with ROCm-enabled containers runs to completion on
  AMD GPU nodes.
- A multi-GPU distributed PyTorchJob runs to completion with all workers on
  AMD GPUs.
- PyTorchJobs requesting `amd.com/gpu` are admitted and run through Kueue
  queueing when enabled.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, partial): PyTorch training on ROCm supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue — the Training Operator / PyTorchJob
  execution side.

## Risks / Notes

- Hardware validation requires AMD Instinct nodes; node availability is an
  externally-controlled availability precondition (strategy open question 1)
  and a coordination risk shared with the validation campaign, not a
  dependency of this epic.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for ROCm workloads

## Description

This epic provides Kueue quota and admission support for the `amd.com/gpu`
resource so that single- and multi-GPU ROCm training jobs are admitted with
correct quota accounting and all-or-nothing (gang) semantics on AMD Instinct
nodes.

## Scope

- Define ClusterQueue/LocalQueue resource-flavor configuration covering the
  `amd.com/gpu` resource on AMD Instinct nodes within the platform's Kueue
  quota model.
- Validate quota enforcement for jobs requesting `amd.com/gpu`: jobs exceeding
  quota remain pending until quota is available.
- Validate all-or-nothing (gang) admission of multi-GPU ROCm jobs requesting
  `amd.com/gpu`, via the platform's waitForPodsReady admission semantics.
- Validate admission of PyTorchJobs requesting `amd.com/gpu` end-to-end with
  the ROCm training job configuration (the job-side runtime work is owned by
  the PyTorch ROCm training workstream; this epic covers the queueing and
  quota side).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Quota configuration supports `amd.com/gpu` resource flavors on AMD Instinct
  node pools.
- A multi-GPU job requesting `amd.com/gpu` is admitted all-or-nothing under
  waitForPodsReady semantics.
- Jobs exceeding the available `amd.com/gpu` quota remain pending until quota
  is available.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, partial): PyTorch training on ROCm supported for single- and
  multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with `amd.com/gpu` quota handling —
  the Kueue queueing/quota side.

## Risks / Notes

- Hardware validation requires AMD Instinct nodes; node availability is an
  externally-controlled availability precondition (strategy open question 1)
  and a coordination risk shared with the validation campaign, not a
  dependency of this epic.

# AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement documentation

## Description

This epic authors the user-facing documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement:
supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list for
ROCm serving, plus guidance for running PyTorch ROCm training jobs with Kueue
quota. Content follows the Red Hat docs content process.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Supported AMD Instinct hardware and driver prerequisites for ROCm serving
  and training.
- The validated model list for the vLLM ROCm serving runtime, matching the
  validation campaign's cleared model list.
- How to deploy and use the vLLM ROCm serving runtime with KServe
  InferenceServices on AMD GPU nodes.
- How to submit single- and multi-GPU PyTorch ROCm training jobs admitted
  through Kueue, including `amd.com/gpu` quota configuration and usage.
- Limitations: GPU sharing/partitioning and non-AMD accelerator families are
  out of scope for enablement.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation topics are published stating the supported AMD hardware,
  driver prerequisites, and the validated model list.
- The documented model list matches the validation campaign's cleared model
  list.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented serving runtime
  and training/quota configuration.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list.
